value.title: China's Envision Energy unveils new AI-powered energy system for remote mine sites
value.snippet: China-based green technology company Envision Energy has unveiled a new AI-powered energy system for the mining and smelting industry, combining wind, solar, battery storage, gas turbines fuelled by green hydrogen/green ammonia, and an integrated dispatch and control system to lower energy costs, ensure reliable power supply and accelerate decarbonisation. The system addresses a central challenge across the mining and smelting sector - building up a hybrid new energy system to deliver affordable but reliable green power supply to remote mining sites with weak or even no grid connections.

value.title: Zambia's President appoints new Mines Minister in Cabinet changes after election
value.snippet: Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema on Wednesday appointed Brenda Tambatamba as the Southern African copper-producing country's new Mines Minister, among Cabinet changes after he won a second term in August's election. Tambatamba served as Labour Minister in Hichilema's previous Cabinet.

value.title: Uranium poised for long-term structural deficit as AI boom spurs unprecedented nuclear demand
value.snippet: With nuclear reactor builds currently outpacing new uranium mine supply and the rapid growth of AI and data centres is reinforcing the need for large-scale baseload power, uranium's investment case does not rest on sentiment, finds Canadian uranium explorer Purecore in an investor report. Drawing on insights from International Energy Agency (IEA), International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), US Energy Information Administration (EIA), Sprott Asset Management and Cameco Corporation, Purecore highlights a timing imbalance between the rapid development of AI infrastructure and the longer development timelines associated with new uranium mines.

value.title: Cash on hand for study plus early mine preparations, Southern Palladium reports
value.snippet: Combined cash and term deposits support the continued advancement of the Bengwenyama platinum group metals (PGMs) project through the definitive feasibility study (DFS) phase and taking in preparations for early mine development, Southern Palladium reported on Wednesday, October 28, when it published its third-quarter production report. The Johannesburg- and Sydney-listed Southern Palladium is developing Bengwenyama in a part of South Africa’s prolific Bushveld Complex known for platinum, palladium, rhodium and chrome richness.

value.title: Swedish high-purity graphite producer Talga inks offtake with Japan's Dainen Materials
value.snippet: Swedish graphite miner Talga Group has signed a binding offtake term sheet with Japan's Dainen Materials for the supply of Talga's Talnode-C high-performance anode material from Sweden. Dainen has been extensively testing Talnode-C against the most rigorous specifications of its Japanese battery customers.

value.title: Lack of gas-supply assurances sees no gas-to-power bidders selected in SA’s first bid window
value.snippet: Electricity and Energy Minister Dr Kgosientsho Ramokgopa has confirmed that none of the four bidders that made submissions under South Africa’s inaugural gas-to-power bidding round has been appointed as a preferred bidder. This, after none of the bidders were able to provide the gas-supply assurances required by the tender. Through the first bid window of the Gas Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme, or GASIPPPP, government was aiming to procure 2 000 MW of generation capacity in line with the country’s Integrated Resource Plan for electricity.

value.title: Forrestania extends takeover offer for Zenith shareholders one last time
value.snippet: As an off-market takeover made by ASX-listed Forrestania Resources for fellow-listed Zenith Minerals extends for another few weeks to November 12, Forrestania has advised that it will not again extend the offer. The offer, which entails one new Forrestania share for every 4.3 Zenith shares held, was first made on June 9 and has been extended ten times owing to orders and corrective disclosures required by the Takeovers Panel.

value.title: Green hydrogen without needing electricity solution selected for French defence funding
value.snippet: A consortium led by French productivity solutions company for hydrogen Novacium, together with open innovation chemistry platform Axel'One and gas engineering company AD-VENTA, have secured funding from the Defence Innovation Agency and the Directorate General of Armaments for the Metagene green hydrogen project. The funding, granted under the French dual-use innovation support programme called RAPID, aims to help the companies develop a self-contained, high-pressure green hydrogen production station using a solid and non-hazardous metallic fuel.

value.title: Deep Sea Minerals appoints new CFO, announces intension to list in US
value.snippet: Canada- and Frankfurt-listed Deep Sea Minerals has appointed Raj Matthew CFO effective immediately. He brings to the seabed mineral exploration and development company more than 25 years of financial leadership experience, including as CFO of networking hardware company Asante Technologies.

value.title: Canadian gold miner Spanish Mountain progresses grid connection study with British Columbia utility
value.snippet: TSX-V-listed emerging gold miner Spanish Mountain Gold has signed a facilities study agreement with British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority to connect the Spanish Mountain gold project to the grid. For president and CEO Peter Mah, the facilities study agreement is a significant milestone toward a construction decision for the project, since secure and reliable grid power is a cornerstone requirement for the operation.

value.title: World Bank sees commodity prices up 23% in 2026 due to Middle East war, other shocks
value.snippet: Global commodity prices are set to surge 23% in 2026, the World Bank said on Wednesday, citing rising energy prices and disruptions to cargo shipping during the Middle East war, grain shipment problems in the Black Sea and high demand for safe-haven assets such as gold. Oil, natural gas, food and metals prices all rose sharply this year as global shocks mounted, the World Bank said in its latest Commodity Markets Outlook. It said the situation could worsen if the conflict in the Middle East ratcheted up and damage to Russian oil infrastructure continued.

value.title: Indian miner Vedanta on track to eliminate net debt by December-end, CEO says
value.snippet: Vedanta is on track to eliminate net debt by the end of the year after lowering it sharply due to strong earnings and cash generation, CEO Arun Misra said on Wednesday. The milestone would cap a years-long deleveraging drive at Vedanta. A net cash position could also boost financial flexibility and reduce borrowing costs as the company pursues growth projects.

value.title: India seeks $220bn clean energy push to meet 2030 target
value.snippet: India needs about $220-billion in clean energy investment over the next three years as it races to expand renewable power and grid infrastructure to meet its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, a senior government official said on Wednesday. Santosh Kumar Sarangi, the top official at the federal clean energy ministry, said the investments will be needed across solar and wind power, battery energy storage, green hydrogen and transmission infrastructure.

value.title: Gem Resources to sell South African emerald mine as its shifts focus to gold processing

The disposal forms part of Gem Resources' strategic repositioning towards operating, revenue-generating natural resources businesses, with an increasing focus on gold processing, including through its conditional acquisition of the El Yarumo gold processing operation, in Cauca, Colombi.

value.title: Appian targets about $2bn for Africa but warns policy risk is driving capital away
value.snippet: Appian Capital Advisory plans to deploy $5-billion to $7-billion globally over the next 12 to 24 months, with roughly $2 billion for Africa, CEO Michael Scherb said, though policy uncertainty is pushing investment toward Latin America. The London-based mining private equity firm currently holds three active investments in Africa and has exited three others. Those exits include projects in Burkina Faso and Tanzania, which came amid a coup and an election crisis, respectively. Appian has four active investments in Latin America, mainly in Brazil.

value.title: Ramaco discusses coal's role in critical minerals, advanced material manufacturing at CIAB

The CIAB is a group of senior executives from coal-related industrial enterprises that provides advice to IEA on a broad range of coal-related issues. Its membership is drawn from more than 10 countries representing almost 80% of global coal production and consumption.

value.title: Steady improvement in South Africa’s mineral exploration landscape reported
value.snippet: While South Africa’s targeted mineral exploration activity has been limited for a decade or two, mining industry professionals participating in a webinar hosted by Creamer Media have reported promising improvements that could drive a resurgence in exploration. The 'Who Really De-Risks Exploration' webinar was held on October 28 and facilitated by events organiser Hyve Investing in African Mining Indaba industry director Laura Nicholson. The panel of speakers were Standard Bank Corporate and Investment Banking metals and mining coverage executive head Thapelo Moamogoe, Minerals Council South Africa junior and emerging miners desk lead Grant Mitchell, Council for Geoscience CEO Mosa Mabuza, mining and water consulting firm SRK Consulting geological and geotechnical consultant and mining business analyst Dr Nicolaas Steenkamp and copper and base metals miner Orion Minerals sustainability and business support executive Marcus Birch.

value.title: Perpetua awarded up to $40m in US Army funding to advance domestic tungsten supply
value.snippet: Nasdaq- and TSX-listed Perpetua Resources has been awarded up to $40-million in funding from the US Army's Defense Ordnance Technology Consortium (DOTC) to fund a programme to evaluate the technical and economic feasibility of producing tungsten concentrate at the historical Stibnite mining district, in Idaho. Structured as a 36-month cost-share programme between the company and the US government, the funding will support drilling to define a potential tungsten mineral resource, collection of material for laboratory and bench-scale metallurgical testing and permitting and engineering of an exploration decline to access areas of known tungsten mineralisation.

value.snippet: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.

value.title: Spain's Abenojar Tungsten makes London market debut in biggest mining IPO since 2018
value.snippet: Spanish miner Abenojar Tungsten made its official market debut on the LSE's main market on Friday, marking the largest mining flotation by funds raised in London since 2018. Unconditional dealings in the shares, trading under the ticker "ABT," began on Friday, following conditional trading that started when the IPO was priced at 110p a share on Tuesday.

value.title: Apollo Silver delivers positive PEA for California project
value.snippet: TSX-V-listed Apollo Silver Corp has reported positive results from a preliminary economic assessment (PEA) at its Calico silver project, California, in the US, with the PEA estimating an after-tax net present value (NPV) of $737-million, an after-tax internal rate of return of 25% and a payback period of three years. The PEA is based on the development of an openpit mining operation at the Waterloo deposit, feeding a conventional 8 000 t/d milling and cyanidation leach plant with an initial planned processing life of about 15 years.

value.title: Wet commissioning under way at Allied Gold’s Kurmuk mine
value.snippet: TSX-listed Allied Gold says mining operations at its Kurmuk gold mine in Ethiopia are progressing well, with mining grades in line with the company’s expectations, and ore stockpiles close to the planned level of about three months of plant feed ahead of the November ramp-up. The company highlights that the Kurmuk gold mine represents the cornerstone of Allied’s production and cash flow growth, thereby delivering a significant increase in production at attractive operating costs while enhancing the scale, quality and longevity of the company’s portfolio.

value.title: Centerra lowers full-year AISC guidance for Mount Milligan

The mine also remains on track to meet its full-year production guidance of 140 000 oz to 155 000 oz of gold and 50-million to 60-million pounds of copper.

value.title: Veramark Assurance launches Responsible Metals Value Chain Platform
value.snippet: Assurance system Veramark Assurance, formerly the Copper Mark, has launched the Responsible Metals Value Chain Platform, a network designed to connect companies and stakeholders across the minerals and metals value chain and support greater transparency, collaboration and responsible production and sourcing.
